text: {"title":"Foreign key placement in one-to-many relationships","body":"First, acknowledge the intuition that the author “owns” the posts, so it feels natural to put a reference on the author side; that expectation is why many students adopt the opposite model. Second, point out the concrete failure: a single column on the author table could only store one post ID, so an author with two posts would have no place to record the second reference. The course material shows the opposite – Django creates an author_id column on the blog_post table (page 83) and the Comment model stores a post foreign key on each comment (page 177), exactly because the many side holds the key. Finally, reinforce the correct model: define the foreign key in the “many” model (Post) as models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE); this generates the foreign‑key column on the many‑side table, allowing any number of posts to point to the same author. Tell students to always look for the column that appears on the table that can have many rows referencing a single parent – that is the reliable indicator of the proper placement."}
